hook: Hyderabad auto drivers call a *day-long* bandh on Nov 30
hook_b: Hyderabad auto drivers call a *day-long* bandh on Nov 30
tldr: The Mahatma Gandhi Telangana Auto Drivers JAC wants revised meter fares implemented within 15 days, or the Transport Minister's resignation, and has called a bandh on Nov 30.

beats.what: Demands include revised meter charges, a ban on green cabs, a crackdown on the auto black market and ₹36,000 per driver (₹12,000 a year) as promised.
beats.why: The JAC says new cab and bike-taxi services are hurting drivers' earnings and that the promised fare revision hasn't come.
beats.care: If the bandh goes ahead, autos may be scarce across the city on Nov 30; plan Metro, bus or cab alternatives.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Siasat (Nov 16): an August strike by the same association was called off after a meeting with the Transport Minister.

cards.q: Should auto meter fares in Hyderabad be revised?

qs: How would revised meter fares change a typical short auto ride?
Could talks before Nov 30 end this like the August strike?

facts.t: Drivers want *₹36,000* each, at ₹12,000 a year, as promised by the government.
They seek *₹10 lakh* for the family of a driver allegedly assaulted in September.

viz.verdict: Drivers seek fare revision; commuters may face a no-auto day

steps.e: Earlier strike called off after talks

watch: Whether talks with the Transport Minister before Nov 30 lead to the bandh being called off, as in August.

fact: Hyderabad's auto drivers have called a *day-long* city bandh on November 30
twist: They also want bike taxis banned in the city, like in Bengaluru.
